summary: 125-ft refuge headquarters lookout built and painted in 1936; listed as removed or gone with no removal date, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 125-foot lookout tower, painted orange and white
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts lists it as removed and the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as Tower Gone; no removal date or cause found

access.note: Refuge grounds open every day from sunrise to sunset; no source describes the former tower site

events.note: 125-foot tower constructed and painted at the Headquarters
December 1936 description calls the tower very spindly and says it moves when a climber steps on the platform

evidence.supports: tower built in 1936 at the Headquarters, 125 feet
evidence.quote: 1936: A 125 foot tower was constructed and painted at the Headquarters.
The 125 ft lookout tower at Headquarters has been painted orange and white

evidence.supports: top painted orange for twenty feet, then a white ten-foot band, then alternating orange and white
evidence.quote: the platform and top was painted orange down for twenty feet, and then a piece white for ten ft., and alternating with orange and white on down

evidence.supports: description quoted from a Region 6 assessment by Lou Ann Speulda
evidence.quote: Region 6: Historical and Architectural Assessment of the Depression Era Works Projects - Lou Ann Speulda

evidence.supports: tower described as very spindly and moving under a climber
evidence.quote: the tower is very spindly and weaves whenever one takes a step on the platform

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts lists the tower as removed
Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the headquarters tower as gone
evidence.quote: Fort Niobrara NWR – HQ Cherry 42.89528 -100.47556 Tower Gone

evidence.supports: about five miles east of Valentine on Highway 12
evidence.quote: Located just 5 miles east of Valentine NE on HWY 12.

evidence.supports: grounds open every day sunrise to sunset; visitor center weekday hours
evidence.quote: Refuge Visitor Center: 8-4 Monday-Friday, excluding federal holidays. Refuge Grounds: Open every day, all year, from sunrise to sunset.

evidence.supports: NPS says visitor center open Memorial Day to Labor Day
evidence.quote: has a Visitor Center that is open Memorial Day-Labor Day
Fort Niobrara National Wildlife Refuge, USFWS.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NPS page says the visitor center is open Memorial Day to Labor Day; the refuge page gives weekday hours. The story reports both and uses the refuge's own hours as current.

notes_for_editor: Only one detailed source (Forest Lookouts) covers this tower; its removal date and cause appear in no source found. The FFLA list only gives status. The NPS and refuge pages disagree on visitor center hours. The HQ coordinate 42.89528, -100.47556 comes from FFLA and is not confirmed against any source about the tower. A different Kemnow page (Big Beaver Creek, 1934, 45 ft, removed) was seen only as a search snippet and is a separate record, so it was not used. No photo found.
